title: DW3 port <topic>/manifest.json (asset-manifest-v1)
description: The manifest of one topic folder of the exported data (data/<topic>/manifest.json, one per topic; mods do not write it). It records which files the exporter wrote and their hash, so a file the user edited is never overwritten. Derived from pc/shim/text_data.c (tdManifestParse, tdManifestFormat: the parser refuses an unknown member, a text after the object, a manifest without format or files, and a version that is not a plain decimal number; a refused manifest counts as absent and the topic is exported again) and the exporters' use of it (pc/shim/exp_core.c). Informational for a modder: do not edit it.

topic.description: The topic folder: partners, digimon, sprites, stages, menus, cards, audio, video, images, text, raw.

exporter.description: Exporter unit -> version (a decimal number without leading zeros). The version goes up when the bytes an exporter writes change; a different number makes the topic export again. The unit is an exporter (partners, menus, stage-data, stage-objects, images, text) or a piece of one versioned apart: a battle bank by name, a fighter by folder (d003), a scene's tiles (stage-tiles/s202), a raw/ kind. A topic two exporters share (stages, menus) has one entry for each.

disc.description: Hash (16 lowercase hex digits) of the disc's volume descriptor and path table; the same in every topic. With another disc the files still belong to the manifest but the versions do not count and the topic is exported again. May be empty.

inputs.description: Optional: other hashes the files depend on. Only text/ writes it: overlay (the es-419 overlay's hash, or none) and disc-text.

names.description: Folder -> identity, such as "c001": "dw3:card/1" (cards/). {} until an exporter has its map.

files.description: Path relative to the topic folder -> hash of the file as the exporter wrote it (FNV-1a 64 bit over the bytes, 16 lowercase hex digits; tdHash in pc/shim/text_data.c). A file whose hash differs is the user's and is kept: the new bytes go to <file>.new.
